bug_description.original: A heap-use-after-free in libxml2's xinclude.c: xmlXIncludeIncludeNode (seen via xmlXIncludeDoProcess/xmlXIncludeLoadFallback) can read memory from XML nodes that have already been freed during XInclude/fallback processing. This use-after-free can cause crashes or memory corruption and may be exploitable.
bug_description.normalized: During fallback reprocessing, libxml2 records an inner xi:include node in an XInclude reference entry by storing the node pointer in `ret->ref` / `ctxt->incTab[*]->ref`. Later, outer include substitution frees that same child node with `xmlFreeNode(child)` but leaves the `incTab` entry intact. A subsequent `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` reloads the dangling pointer with `cur = ctxt->incTab[nr]->ref` and dereferences the freed node, causing a heap use-after-free read.

source.value_from: The attacker-controlled testcase is parsed into a DOM containing nested xi:include and xi:fallback nodes, and the fallback node from that DOM is passed here for recursive XInclude processing.
source.description: Fallback handling consumes the attacker-shaped fallback subtree and starts recursive XInclude processing on it.

root_cause.description: The preprocessing path preserves the traversed fallback-child xi:include node by storing its pointer in the XInclude reference entry as `ret->ref`, which is then kept in `ctxt->incTab[*]` and later survives after that node is freed.

sink.description: A later xmlXIncludeIncludeNode reloads the dangling node from `ctxt->incTab[nr]->ref` and immediately dereferences the freed xmlNode in the guard on `cur->type`, which is the first project read on the stale pointer in the crashing call.

tainted_value_origin.value_from: The testcase shapes the fallback subtree so it contains an inner xi:include that is both recorded in `incTab` during fallback recursion and later freed when the outer include removes fallback children.
tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker controls the DOM subtree whose nodes become the later-stored and later-freed xmlNode pointers.

parser_admitted.description: The XML parser admits the testcase and starts building element nodes for the attacker-supplied document that contains the nested xi:include and xi:fallback structure.

admitted_location.code: ret = xmlNewDocNodeEatName(ctxt->myDoc, ctxt->node, pref, lname, NULL);

fine_trace.note: Fallback processing starts recursive XInclude traversal on the attacker-controlled fallback element with skipRoot enabled.
Because skipRoot is set, traversal begins at `fallback->children`, making the inner xi:include child the current node examined for preprocessing.
Preprocessing passes the traversed inner xi:include node into XInclude reference creation so it will be retained in the processing context.
Reference creation stores the current xi:include node pointer in the new XInclude entry as `ret->ref`, preserving an alias to that DOM node inside `ctxt->incTab[*]`.
The reference object containing `ret->ref` is inserted into `ctxt->incTab`, making the alias reachable for later load/include passes.

fine_trace.code: for (child = cur->children; child != NULL; child = next) {
fine_trace.note: When the outer xi:include is later substituted, the code iterates over its fallback children, including the same inner xi:include node whose pointer was stored in `ctxt->incTab[*]->ref`.
The outer include removes a fallback child by unlinking and freeing that xmlNode, but the corresponding `ctxt->incTab[*]->ref` alias is not cleared.

A later include pass reloads the node pointer from `ctxt->incTab[nr]->ref`; because that entry still aliases the freed child, `cur` becomes a dangling xmlNode pointer before the function checks and dereferences it.
The function dereferences the dangling `cur` immediately in the guard on `cur->type`, and then continues into the `inc`/`xptr` branch at line 2218, which matches the ASan read in this re-entry path.

format.contract: The input must parse into nested XInclude markup where an outer `xi:include` has an `xi:fallback` subtree containing an inner `xi:include`, so fallback recursion records the inner include in `incTab` and outer include substitution later frees that same fallback child before the stored `ref` is reloaded.
format.name: xml

poc.trigger: The saved OSS-Fuzz testcase must parse into nested XInclude markup that drives `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback` to reprocess an `xi:fallback` subtree with `skipRoot=1`, records an inner `xi:include` node into `ctxt->incTab[*]->ref`, then later frees that same child during outer include substitution before a later `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` reloads the stale `ref`.

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 used only the staged vulnerable source, patch diff, saved sanitizer trace, and reproduction report; it did not rerun the target or add runtime probes.
The exact testcase layout is inferred from the saved XInclude control flow and issue description rather than re-executed document dumps in this stage.
